speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what are the criteria used to determine childcare and preschool subsidies; and (b) when were these criteria last reviewed.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In reviewing the affordability of preschools for families, we take into account fee levels in the preschool sector; household needs and incomes; as well as various Government schemes, apart from direct subsidies, which contribute to the affordability of preschools.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These are available for all Singapore Citizen children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In 2013, the Government reviewed childcare subsidies to better support low- to middle-income families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Lower-income families and larger families receive more subsidy.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Together with the Basic Subsidy, a low-income family can pay as little as a few dollars a month for preschool.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Kindergartens offer shorter focused education programmes and are generally more affordable, with a median fee of $170 today.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Parents can tap on these measures to help pay for part of the needs of their children, including healthcare and preschool.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In addition, we will continue to make good quality preschool affordable through MOE Kindergartens, as well as preschools under the AOP and Partner Operator (POP) schemes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Fees that preschools under the AOP and POP schemes can charge are subject to fee caps, to remain affordable.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Through these series of measures, we seek to keep preschool services affordable, especially to middle- and lower-income households.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will continue to review our policies to ensure that quality preschool remains accessible and affordable for families.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Indeed, it is heartening to see that the Government has been making progress in the area of supporting parents from different socioeconomic status in the course of their journey as parents.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: First of all, could the Minister shed some light, in light of perhaps changing circumstances and the rising cost of living, on when the next review of subsidies would be due?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My second question is to perhaps assess the support that is given to non-working mothers or mothers who are working part-time.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I do understand the logic that when the parents are working full-time that, therefore, they would need the support of childcare.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But in some of my visits and interactions with the residents, the feedback I have received is that there could be many reasons why a parent chooses to work part-time or is unable to work, and it does not necessarily mean that they require any less support with regard to quality childcare and quality early childhood education.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope the Minister could shed some light on these two areas.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I have articulated earlier, there are both the direct subsidies to the child but also the indirect measures, such as through the Baby Bonus and CDA policies which were only recently amended, a couple of years ago, as well as the subsidies to operators to help them keep fees low and affordable for Singaporean children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On the Member's second point, the purpose of tiering the basic subsidies and additional subsidies in the way that we have articulated earlier is to provide support to mothers who work and, therefore, need full-day childcare.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For those who do not work or who work part-time, there is the possibility of putting their children in half-day kindergarten services.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Having said that, the Member is quite right that there are a variety of reasons that may prevent a mother from going to work full-time and, hence, benefiting directly from these subsidies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Early Childhood Development Agency will look at all appeals on a case-by-case basis and we have given exemptions to those who can provide reasons to the childcare centre and with supporting documents, such as retrenchments, and through health reasons or their other caregiving obligations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, certainly, we want to support not just working mothers but mothers who may, for various circumstances and exigencies, be unable to do so and, therefore, need support for childcare.
